official_sources: Planning Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas Act 1990
Local authority listed building consent guidance

official_measurement_examples.name: Current national collection
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data reported 382,254 listed-building records; collector last ran and new data was found on 24 July 2026.

official_measurement_examples.name: Point limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The listed-building dataset says its point does not define the extent of the area affected by listing.

official_measurement_examples.name: Outline limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The listed-building-outline dataset is incomplete and does not consistently show listed-building curtilage, so it is indicative only.

official_measurement_examples.name: Grade separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Grades I, II* and II are significance categories and are not automatic planning outcomes.

official_measurement_examples.name: Consent separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Listed building consent is a separate statutory consent from planning permission and both may be required for the same proposal.

official_measurement_examples.name: Curtilage assessment
official_measurement_examples.fact: Curtilage-listed status cannot be derived solely from a national derivative polygon and requires legal and factual assessment.

official_measurement_examples.name: Temporal status
official_measurement_examples.fact: Historic/out-of-date listed-building entities retain end-date context and must not be silently treated as current.

official_measurement_examples.name: Parcel limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Listing does not establish ownership, access rights, exact buildable area or development yield.

core_rules: listed-building point is not legal extent
curtilage cannot be inferred solely from outline geometry
listed building consent is separate from planning permission
planning permission is not listed building consent
grade is not automatic planning outcome
internal works may require LBC without planning permission
works near a listed building are not automatically within listing
historic entity status must retain end date
NHLE legal designation takes precedence over derivative data
designation does not calculate development yield
absence from derivative outline is not proof of no curtilage effect
locally listed building is distinct from nationally listed building
no parcel heritage clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official Planning Data, Historic England, GOV.UK and legislation sources checked on 2026-07-26. July 2026 collection status and point/outline/curtilage/consent distinctions were retained; no parcel promotion.
